mcqs.question: For the inequality 3x - 5 > 7, which of the following best describes its solution set?
mcqs.explanation: Solving 3x - 5 > 7 gives 3x > 12, so x > 4. Hence the solution set consists of all real numbers greater than 4. Option B states this correctly; the other options describe opposite or inclusive relations.

mcqs.question: A student has scored 45 marks in internal assessment. Each additional practice test adds 5 marks. To obtain at least 70 marks overall, what is the minimum number of practice tests the student must take?
mcqs.explanation: Let n be the number of practice tests. The total marks are 45 + 5n \ge 70. Subtracting 45 gives 5n \ge 25, so n \ge 5. The smallest integer satisfying this is 5. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they give totals below 70 or exceed the minimum required.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent solutions on a number line
mcqs.question: Which of the following number‑line representations correctly shows the solution set of the inequality x \le -2?

options.A: An open circle at -2 with an arrow pointing left
options.B: A closed circle at -2 with an arrow pointing left
options.C: A closed circle at -2 with an arrow pointing right
options.D: An open circle at -2 with an arrow pointing right

mcqs.answer: A closed circle at -2 with an arrow pointing left
mcqs.explanation: The inequality x \le -2 includes the endpoint -2, so the circle must be closed, and all numbers less than -2 are included, so the arrow points left. Option B matches this. Option A excludes -2, option C points to the wrong side, and option D both excludes -2 and points the wrong way.

mcqs.question: What is the solution set of the inequality -3 < 2x + 1 \le 5 expressed in interval notation?
mcqs.explanation: First, -3 < 2x + 1 gives -4 < 2x, so x > -2. Next, 2x + 1 \le 5 gives 2x \le 4, so x \le 2. Combining, -2 < x \le 2, which is written as (-2, 2]. Option C matches this; the other options either exclude 2 or include -2 incorrectly.

mcqs.question: Consider the two inequalities (i) 2x - 3 > 1 and (ii) 4x + 5 \le 13. Which statement about their solution sets is true?

options.A: Both inequalities have the same solution set.
options.B: The two solution sets have no common elements.
options.C: Their union consists of all real numbers greater than 2.
options.D: Their intersection consists of the single point x = 2.

mcqs.answer: The two solution sets have no common elements.
mcqs.explanation: Inequality (i) simplifies to x > 2. Inequality (ii) simplifies to x \le 2. There is no real number that is simultaneously greater than 2 and less than or equal to 2, so the intersection is empty, making statement B true. Statement A is false because the sets are different. Statement C is false because the union actually includes all real numbers (both x > 2 and x \le 2). Statement D is false because x = 2 satisfies only the second inequality, not the first.

mcqs.question: For what value of the parameter a does the inequality 2x - a < 5 have the solution set x < 3?
mcqs.explanation: Rewrite the inequality: 2x - a < 5 \Rightarrow 2x < 5 + a \Rightarrow x < (5 + a)/2. For this to be equivalent to x < 3, we need (5 + a)/2 = 3, giving 5 + a = 6 and a = 1. Hence option C is correct; the other values give different boundary points.

mcqs.question: Solve the inequality 4 - 3x \le 10.
mcqs.explanation: Subtract 4 from both sides: -3x \le 6. Divide by -3 (remember to reverse the inequality sign): x \ge -2. Option B states this correctly; the other options either reverse the direction or use a strict inequality.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent solutions on a number line
mcqs.question: A number line shows a closed circle at 0 with an arrow extending to the right. Which algebraic description matches this representation?
mcqs.explanation: A closed circle at 0 indicates that 0 is included in the solution set, and the arrow to the right shows all numbers greater than 0 are also included. Therefore the set is x \ge 0. Option D captures this; options A and C exclude 0, and option B includes numbers less than 0, which does not match the arrow direction.
